summary: Marshall Memorial Municipal Airport is a small general aviation facility serving Marshall, a city in Saline County in west-central Missouri. The airport primarily supports private pilots, flight training, and recreational flying, with no scheduled commercial service. It features a single asphalt runway and basic amenities catering to the local aviation community in this rural Midwestern region.
faqs:
Q: Does Marshall Memorial Municipal Airport offer commercial flights?
A: No, this is a general aviation airport with no scheduled commercial airline service.

Q: What is the primary use of the airport?
A: The airport primarily serves private pilots, recreational flyers, flight training, and general aviation activities.

Q: How many runways does KMHL have?
A: The airport has a single asphalt runway suitable for small to mid-size general aviation aircraft.

Q: Are there fuel services available at the airport?
A: General aviation airports like this typically offer basic fuel and services, but pilots should confirm availability with the airport manager before arrival.
transport_tips: Reaching the airport from Marshall town center requires a personal vehicle, as there is no public transit serving the facility. The airport is located a short drive northwest of downtown Marshall along US-65, making road access straightforward. Travelers flying in should arrange ground transportation or rental car service in advance, as on-site rental options are unlikely.
local_tip: Frequent visitors recommend contacting the airport manager ahead of time for after-hours access, as the facility may have limited staffing outside business hours typical of small municipal airports.
